scope: Corollary 5.1 (Gaussian maxima) of the manuscript “The Gaussian propeller bound in every dimension” (preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 096 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b546ae5fd2ea7011), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let d, k be positive integers, let g be standard Gaussian in Rd, and let v1, . . . , vk ∈ Rd, with v̄ = k−1 Pk i=1 vi. Then E max 1≤i≤k ⟨vi, g⟩ ≤ 3 2 √ 2π k X i=1 ∥vi − v̄∥2 !1/2 . The constant is sharp already for three vectors in the plane.
